This is deliberate — it prevents an LLM from flipping the toggle on itself mid-task.\n\n2. **Secret redaction is OFF by default** — Tool output passes through unmodified. If you need API keys and secrets masked, run `hermes config set security.redact_secrets true` and restart. This does NOT affect `approvals.mode` — they are independent settings.\n\n3. **YOLO mode is NOT safe for secrets** — Setting `approvals.mode: off` or `--yolo` disables command approval but does NOT disable secret redaction. They do NOT apply mid-conversation to preserve prompt caching. Tell users this explicitly.\n\n5. **Cron jobs run in a fresh session** — Cron cron-run sessions have no current-chat context. Prompts must be fully self-contained. Skills and context_from are the only way to inject prior state.\n\n6. **Script-based cron jobs expect scripts in the profile's scripts/ directory** — Not `~/.hermes/scripts/`. The scheduler looks for scripts at `~/.hermes/profiles/<profile>/scripts/<name>.sh`.\n\n7. **tmux sessions persist after Claude Code exits** — If Claude Code crashes or is killed mid-session, the tmux session remains. Always clean up with `tmux kill-session -t <name>` when done.\n\n8. **Gateway auth requires browser** — OAuth verification codes pasted via tmux `send-keys` fail because tmux treats them as password input. The user must log in on their local machine with a browser for initial auth.\n\n9. **Print mode can't write files** — Claude Code in `-p` mode refuses file writes. Use shell redirect (`> output.md 2>&1`) or the `write_file` tool instead.\n\n10. **Fable 5 session token budget** — Fable 5 has a per-session token budget. Running multiple parallel Fable 5 jobs can exhaust the budget mid-run. Run them sequentially or with max 2 concurrent.\n\n11. **Session resumption requires same directory** — `--continue` only works in the same working directory. For cross-directory work, capture the session ID and resume explicitly.\n\n12. **Context degradation is real** — AI output quality measurably degrades above 70% context window usage. Monitor with `/context` and proactively `/compact`.\n\n13. **`/exit` opens agent selector in OpenCode** — It's NOT a valid exit command. Use Ctrl+C to exit OpenCode sessions.\n\n14. **OpenCode needs `pty=true` for interactive mode** — OpenCode is a TUI app. Without PTY, it hangs. `opencode run` (bounded tasks) does NOT need PTY.\n\n15. **OAuth tokens are stored in `~/.hermes/auth.json`** — If auth is failing, check this file. completeness\n7. **Documentation**: Create final markdown files in knowledge repository\n8. **Version Control**: Commit and push changes to GitHub\n\n## Detailed Steps\n\n### 1. Source Preparation\n\n```bash\n# Create workspace for extraction\nmkdir -p /tmp/knowledge_extraction\ncd /tmp/knowledge_extraction\n\n# Save source URLs for reference. For batches, include a human label per URL.\ncat > sources.txt << 'EOF'\nDocker concepts | https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ObhdD49AEYw\nAI Server setup with Proxmox | https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kB9a5nXCwkA\nEOF\n```\n\nFor YouTube batches destined for `jordatech/knowledge_extraction`, use the `youtube-content` skill's `references/batch-youtube-knowledge-extraction.md` artifact pattern: one folder per video under `youtube_logs/videos/<VIDEO_ID>/`, plus a batch index linking all final `extracted_knowledge.md` files.\n\n### 2. Fabric-Based Knowledge Extraction\n\nUse fabric patterns to extract structured knowledge:\n\n```bash\n# Install fabric if not present (if needed)\n# curl -sSL https://github.com/danielmiessler/fabric/releases/latest/download/fabric-linux-amd64 -o /usr/local/bin/fabric\n# chmod +x /usr/local/bin/fabric\n\n# Extract knowledge using YouTube transcript pattern\n# Note: This assumes youtube-transcript-api or similar is available\npython3 -c \"\nimport requests\nimport re\nfrom urllib.parse import urlparse, parse_qs\n\ndef extract_video_id(url):\n    parsed_url = urlparse(url)\n    if parsed_url.hostname in ['youtu.be', 'www.youtu.be']:\n        return parsed_url.path[1:]\n    if parsed_url.hostname in ['www.youtube.com', 'youtube.com']:\n        if parsed_url.path == '/watch':\n            return parse_qs(parsed_url.query)['v'][0]\n        if parsed_url.path[:7] == '/embed/':\n            return parsed_url.path.split('/')[2]\n        if parsed_url.path[:3] == '/v/':\n            return parsed_url.path.split('/')[2]\n    return None\n\n# Process each source\nwith open('sources.txt', 'r') as f:\n    urls = [line.strip() for line in f if line.strip()]\n\nfor url in urls:\n    video_id = extract_video_id(url)\n    print(f'Processing video: {video_id}')\n    # In real implementation, would fetch transcript and extract knowledge\n\"\n```\n\n### 3. Knowledge Structure Template\n\nEach extracted knowledge unit should follow this structure:\n\n```markdown\n# [Concept Title]\n\n**Source**: [Video Title] ([URL])\n**Timestamp**: [HH:MM:SS] \n**Extracted On**: [DATE]\n\n## Core Concept\n[Clear, concise explanation of the concept in 1-2 sentences]\n\n## Key Points\n- [Bullet point 1]\n- [Bullet point 2]\n- [Bullet point 3]\n\n## Technical Details\n[Any specific commands, configurations, or technical specifications]\n\n## Practical Application\n[How this knowledge can be applied in real scenarios]\n\n## Related Concepts\n- [Link to related concept 1]\n- [Link to related concept 2]\n\n## Questions & Limitations\n[Open questions or limitations of this knowledge]\n```\n\n### 4. Source-Specific Extraction Guidance\n\nKeep the main skill class-level. When a source family needs narrow guidance, put those notes in `references/` rather than expanding `SKILL.md` with one-session examples.\n\nFor technical video examples such as Docker concepts, Proxmox AI server setup, and local AI server/Open WebUI walkthroughs, see `references/topic-specific-video-guidelines.md`. Adapt those examples to the current source instead of forcing every extraction into those categories.\n\nFor server/workstation/GPU-host procurement research that must produce durable markdown with multiple bill-of-materials options, used/new purchase links, local operating-cost considerations, and explicit budget/use-case alignment, see `references/hardware-bom-research-and-procurement.md`.\n\n### 5. Documentation Standards\n\nAll extracted knowledge should be stored in the `knowledge_extracted` repository with:\n\n- **File Naming**: `{topic}-{specific-concept}.md` (e.g., `docker-container-lifecycle.md`)\n- **Frontmatter**: Include metadata for organization\n- **Tagging**: Use consistent tags for cross-referencing\n- **Linking**: Use relative links to connect related concepts\n- **Versioning**: Commit regularly with descriptive messages\n\n### 6. Quality Assurance\n\nBefore committing extracted knowledge:\n- [ ] Verify technical accuracy against source\n- [ ] Check for completeness of explanation\n- [ ] Ensure proper attribution and timestamps\n- [ ] Validate any code snippets or commands\n- [ ] Confirm formatting matches repository standards\n- [ ] Check for duplicate or overlapping content\n\n### 7. Repository Management\n\nUse the github-repo-management skill to:\n- Clone/create the knowledge_extracted repository\n- Create feature branches for extraction sessions\n- Commit extracted knowledge files\n- Push changes to remote\n- Create pull requests for review (if applicable)\n\nIf GitHub authentication is unavailable at push time, do **not** discard or leave unstaged work: validate artifacts, commit locally on the bot branch, attempt the push once, then report the exact auth blocker and the `git push origin <branch>` command for the user to run after credentials are restored.\n\n### 8. Attachment-Based Research Packages\n\nWhen the user supplies a prompt/document plus an archive and asks for researched markdown answers in a repository, follow `references/attachment-research-package-workflow.md`: extract to `/tmp`, inspect inventory/headings, redact secrets before committing, split broad research into durable topic files, include a sources/caveats file, run a simple secret scan, then commit/push on the correct branch.\n\n## Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them\n\n1. **Loss of Context**: Always include timestamps and source references\n   - Solution: Extract with timestamps immediately when reviewing\n\n2. **Over-extraction**: Getting too granular and losing the forest for the trees\n   - Solution: Focus on concepts that are reusable and actionable\n\n3. **Under-extraction**: Missing important nuances or prerequisites\n   - Solution: Review extraction against source multiple times\n\n4. **Inconsistent Formatting**: Different styles making knowledge hard to consume\n   - Solution: Use templates and linting tools\n\n5. **Attribution Errors**: Failing to properly credit sources\n   - Solution: Capture source info before starting extraction\n\n6. **Knowledge Silos**: Extracting without connecting to existing knowledge\n   - Solution: Always search for related concepts before finalizing\n\n## Templates and This file is always managed — it is refreshed with the bundle even when `../SKILL.md` has been customized.\n4|\n5|Shared protocol (environment, auth, idempotency, dry-run, polling, and error handling) lives in `../SKILL.md`.\n6|\n7|## Workflow Guidance\n8|\n9|Use this reference to collect structured public data for research, monitoring, lead preparation, and content analysis.\n10|\n11|### Match the business outcome\n12|\n13|| Outcome | Start with | Continue with |\n14|| --- | --- | --- |\n15|| Extract a site or document | `/v1/scrape/website` or `/v1/scrape/pdf` | Follow discovered pages only when the task needs them |\n16|| Research developers or software | `/v1/scrape/github/search` | GitHub repository, profile, issues, pulls, contents, or commits |\n17|| Research people, companies, or hiring | LinkedIn people, company, or jobs endpoints | LinkedIn profile or posts for deeper context |\n18|| Research creators and content | `/v1/scrape/youtube/search` | YouTube transcript, channel, or shorts |\n19|| Monitor conversations and audience response | X/Twitter, Reddit, or Instagram search/list endpoints | User, posts, replies, or comments |\n20|| Research advertising | `/v1/scrape/facebook/ads` | Go deep: competitor `pages` plus keyword queries, `activeStatus: \"all\"`, `maxItems` 100+ (see the Meta Ads recipe below) |\n21|| Find local businesses and places | `/v1/scrape/google/places` | Narrow by location and category; set `maxItems: 1` when looking up one specific business (much faster and cheaper) |\n22|\n23|### Recommended workflow\n24|\n25|1. Define the entities and fields the final output needs.\n26|2. Use the dedicated platform endpoint. Never replace it with open-web search.\n27|3. Discover identifiers first, then call detail endpoints only for relevant results.\n28|4. Size `maxItems` to the job, not to caution: on cheap per-item endpoints (Meta ads ~$0.003 per ad) request 100+, and continue with returned page tokens whenever the task needs more.\n29|5. Preserve source URLs and report missing, private, blocked, or partial data honestly.\n30|\n31|### Important constraints\n32|\n33|- Do not send a GitHub token or OAuth credential; DeepAPI handles GitHub authentication server-side and returns public resources only.\n34|- Website and PDF extraction requires public URLs. PDFs must have a readable text layer; image-only scans are not OCRed.\n35|- Bound large pages, documents, and transcripts with `maxChars` or `maxPages`. A `truncated: true` result reached that cap.\n36|- Continue pagination by returning `nextPageToken` unchanged as `pageToken` with the same filters. GitHub profile repository pagination additionally requires `includeRepos: true` and one username.\n37|\n38|### Meta Ads Library research recipe (`/v1/scrape/facebook/ads`)\n39|\n40|One call is not research. Ads cost ~$0.003 each, so depth costs cents while shallow results are worthless. For competitor or market research, fan out 3-5 calls and merge:\n41|\n42|- Run BOTH kinds of calls: `pages` for each competitor (returns everything an advertiser runs) and keyword `query` calls (keyword search only matches ad text, so it misses ads that never mention the term).\n43|- Always set `activeStatus: \"all\"` when researching: inactive ads reveal what an advertiser tested and stopped.\n44|- Vary keywords across calls: brand name, product name, tagline, category term.\n45|- When specific markets matter, query 2-3 key `country` codes in separate calls instead of relying on `ALL` — per-country searches can surface ads that `ALL` misses.\n46|- Request `maxItems` 100+ per call, then dedupe the merged results by ad `id`.\n47|\n48|### Go-deep recipes (high-value patterns)\n49|\n50|Per-item prices are cents or fractions of cents — depth is cheap and shallow results are worthless. Default patterns:\n51|\n52|- X/Twitter monitoring: run `sort: \"latest\"` AND `sort: \"top\"` plus 2-3 query phrasings, `maxItems` 100 each, then dedupe by tweet `id`. Enrich accounts in batches: `/v1/scrape/twitter/user` takes a handle list in one call, with optional `includeFollowers`/`includeFollowing` extraction.\n53|- Websites: pass a URL list to fetch many pages in one `/v1/scrape/website` call, or hand it one deep seed URL to crawl a whole docs/blog subtree — never fetch research pages one call at a time.\n54|- YouTube topics and creators: pull 25 search results or 30 channel videos, then transcript the top 5-10 relevant videos (~$0.02 each) with `/v1/scrape/youtube/transcript` — transcribing 10 videos costs ~$0.20.\n55|- LinkedIn lists: people search exists to build lists — ask for 50+ profiles per call, fan out titles x locations variants, then enrich the shortlist with `/v1/scrape/linkedin/profile`.\n56|\n57|### Reading a `/v1/scrape/website` response\n58|\n59|- `output` is an array of page objects. Each returned page carries the requested content (`markdown` and/or `text`, per `contentFormat`) and, when the origin reports it, a `url`. A page with no extractable content is dropped, so it never appears as a content-free result.\n60|- Per-page metadata fields are optional and present only when available: `title`, `description`, and `language` appear only when the page provides them; `truncated` and `totalChars` appear only on a page that hit the `maxChars` cap. Never assume a field exists; read defensively.\n61|- Follow the polling `next` (a `GET` of `/v1/requests/{requestId}`) whenever it is present, regardless of `status`. A billed run whose content is still settling returns `status: \"succeeded\"` with `output: null`, no `list`, and a polling `next`; poll it until it is absent before treating the result as complete. Do not stop polling just because `status` is no longer `running`, and never auto-follow a `POST` `next` (dry-run execution or paid pagination).\n62|- Read the `list.listState` signal beside `output` to tell an empty fetch from real pages: `results` (pages returned), `no_results` (the origin answered but returned nothing usable), or `source_blocked` (blocking was the dominant reason, for example an HTTP 401, 403, 407, 429, 451, or 503, or a login wall, captcha, rate limit, or access-denied notice). When the origin answers but returns nothing usable the fetch is free (`debitMicrousd: 0`) and `output` is an empty array.\n63|- A run can also end `status: \"failed\"` (for example a backend failure with no working fallback). A failed run is not a free empty success; surface the error instead of treating it as no content.\n64|\n65|### Find exact endpoint details\n66|\n67|- `GET /v1/capabilities` lists every available capability and slug.\n68|- `GET /v1/capabilities?capability=<slug>` returns the exact current schema, example, pricing, and availability for one endpoint.\n69|- `https://deepapi.co/docs/reference.md` is the complete agent-readable API reference.\n70|- `https://deepapi.co/docs/pricing.md` has current endpoint pricing.\n71|- `https://deepapi.co/openapi.json` is the machine-readable contract; `https://deepapi.co/llms.txt` indexes all public agent docs.\n72|", "total_lines": 71, "file_size": 6911, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}

This file carries the full per-endpoint detail.\n6|\n7|## Workflow Guidance\n8|\n9|Use browser automation only when the outcome requires interaction with a public website.\n10|\n11|### Recommended workflow\n12|\n13|1. Prefer the scraping workflow for static reading and extraction.\n14|2. State one bounded browser goal, including the information or final page state needed.\n15|3. Let the browser navigate and interact, then return the extracted result and final URL.\n16|4. Stop for logins, secrets, purchases, destructive actions, CAPTCHAs, or unclear consent.\n17|\n18|## Endpoint Details\n19|\n20|## Browser Task\n21|\n22|`POST /v1/browser/act`\n23|\n24|Run a goal-driven task in a real cloud browser and return its result.\n25|\n26|- Capability: `browser.act`\n27|- Scope: `browser:act`\n28|- Side effects: Performs real actions on public websites and debits credits when the task finishes.\n29|- Cost: Defaults to maxCostUsd 1.00. Finished tasks are billed per attempt, including tasks with isSuccess false. Failed and stopped tasks are free. Typical price: ~$0.10-$0.60 per task depending on steps.\n30|- Idempotency-Key: required\n31|- Polling: If the response carries a polling next action (a GET of /v1/requests/{requestId}), wait next.afterSecs and call it. Keep following that polling next while it is present, even when status is already succeeded (a settling run returns succeeded with output null and a polling next). The result is final when no polling next remains or status is failed. Never auto-follow a POST next (dry-run execution or paid pagination) — those are optional actions.\n32|\n33|Safety:\n34|- Public web only: tasks that need logins, credentials, account creation, CAPTCHA solving, or purchases are rejected.\n35|- Describe one concrete goal per task and set startUrl when you know the site.\n36|\n37|Request body schema:\n38|```json\n39|{\n40|  \"type\": \"object\",\n41|  \"required\": [\n42|    \"task\"\n43|  ],\n44|  \"properties\": {\n45|    \"task\": {\n46|      \"type\": \"string\",\n47|      \"maxLength\": 10000,\n48|      \"description\": \"What to do in the browser, in plain English. Defaults to 25, maximum 50.\"\n61|    },\n62|    \"outputSchema\": {\n63|      \"type\": \"object\",\n64|      \"additionalProperties\": true,\n65|      \"description\": \"Optional JSON Schema for a structured result.\"\n66|    },\n67|    \"allowedDomains\": {\n68|      \"type\": \"array\",\n69|      \"minItems\": 1,\n70|      \"maxItems\": 20,\n71|      \"items\": {\n72|        \"type\": \"string\"\n73|      },\n74|      \"description\": \"Optional allowed domains, like example.com or *.example.com.\"\n75|    },\n76|    \"maxCostUsd\": {\n77|      \"type\": \"string\",\n78|      \"pattern\": \"^\\\\d+(\\\\.\\\\d{1,6})?$\",\n79|      \"default\": \"1.00\",\n80|      \"description\": \"Optional customer spend cap in USD. Defaults to 1.00.\"\n81|    },\n82|    \"maxCostMicrousd\": {\n83|      \"type\": \"integer\",\n84|      \"minimum\": 1,\n85|      \"description\": \"Optional customer spend cap in USD micro-dollars.\"\n86|    },\n87|    \"dryRun\": {\n88|      \"type\": \"boolean\",\n89|      \"default\": false,\n90|      \"description\": \"Zero-spend preview: validate this request and return the exact credit hold it would place (status dry_run plus an estimate object) without reserving, charging, or running anything.\"\n91|    }\n92|  },\n93|  \"additionalProperties\": false\n94|}\n95|```\n96|\n97|Response schema:\n98|```json\n99|{\n100|  \"$ref\": \"#/components/schemas/PublicEnvelope\"\n101|}\n102|```\n103|\n104|Example request body:\n105|```json\n106|{\n107|  \"task\": \"Find the support email address on example.com.\",\n108|  \"startUrl\": \"https://example.com\",\n109|  \"maxCostUsd\": \"1.00\"\n110|}\n111|```\n112|", "total_lines": 111, "file_size": 4094, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}
